f.title: Apply the new definition of nonclinical test and nonclinical study (21 CFR 312.3)
f.statement: 21 CFR 312.3(b) is amended to define 'nonclinical test' and 'nonclinical study' as a test or study conducted in vitro, in silico or in chemico, or a nonhuman in vivo test or study, which may include cell-based assays, organ chips and microphysiological systems, computer modeling, other nonhuman or human biology-based methods such as bioprinting, and animal tests or studies.
f.clause: Amendatory text - PART 312, § 312.3 Definitions and interpretations
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: Nonclinical test and nonclinical study mean a test or study conducted in vitro, in silico, or in chemico, or a nonhuman in vivo test or study. Such test or study may include the following: (1) Cell-based assays. (2) Organ chips and microphysiological systems. (3) Computer modeling. (4) Other nonhuman or human biology-based test methods, such as bioprinting. (5) Animal tests or studies.
rows.location: Amendatory text - PART 312, § 312.3 Definitions and interpretations
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: Review all safety information including nonclinical studies (21 CFR 312.32(b))
f.statement: 21 CFR 312.32(b), which requires the sponsor to promptly review all information relevant to the safety of the drug from foreign or domestic sources, is amended to list 'nonclinical studies' instead of 'animal or in vitro studies' among the sources; FDA states this does not expand the scope of review but clarifies that information from nonclinical studies, including modern methods such as computer modeling and organ chips, is included.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 11. Section 312.32(b)
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: Paragraph 312.32(b) requires the sponsor to “promptly review all information relevant to the safety of the drug obtained or otherwise received by the sponsor from foreign or domestic sources, including information derived from any clinical or epidemiological investigations, animal or in vitro studies, reports in the scientific literature, and unpublished scientific papers, as well as reports from foreign regulatory authorities and reports of foreign commercial marketing experience for drugs that are not marketed in the United States.” We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “animal or in vitro studies” with the phrase “nonclinical studies.”
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 11. Section 312.32(b)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: Report nonclinical findings suggesting significant human risk in IND safety reports within 15 days
f.statement: 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iii) is amended so that the sponsor must report any findings from nonclinical testing (previously 'animal or in vitro testing'), whether or not conducted by the sponsor, that suggest a significant risk in humans exposed to the drug (e.g., mutagenicity, teratogenicity, carcinogenicity, significant organ toxicity at or near expected exposure), in an IND safety report to FDA and all participating investigators as soon as possible and no later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor determines the information qualifies for reporting.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 12. Section 312.32(c)(1)(iii)
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor determines the information qualifies for reporting
rows.quote: Section 312.32(c) requires a sponsor to notify FDA and all participating investigators “of potential serious risks, from clinical trials or any other source” in a safety report provided as soon as possible (but not later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor determines that the information qualifies for reporting under the regulation). Section 312.32(c)(1)(iii) is headed “Findings from animal or in vitro testing.” The first sentence of the paragraph states: “The sponsor must report any findings from animal or in vitro testing, whether or not conducted by the sponsor, that suggest a significant risk in humans exposed to the drug, such as reports of mutagenicity, teratogenicity, or carcinogenicity, or reports of significant organ toxicity at or near the expected human exposure.” We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “animal or in vitro” with the word “nonclinical” in both the heading and first sentence.
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 12. Section 312.32(c)(1)(iii)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the sponsor determines that the information qualifies for reporting
deadline_rule.applies_to: IND safety reports of nonclinical findings suggesting significant risk in humans

f.title: Submit overall findings and pooled analyses from nonclinical studies in narrative format
f.statement: 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(v) is amended so that reports of overall findings or pooled analyses from published and unpublished nonclinical (previously 'in vitro, animal'), epidemiological or clinical studies must be submitted in a narrative format.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 13. Section 312.32(c)(1)(v)
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: Section 312.32(c)(1)(v) describes the format in which sponsors must submit IND safety reports and contains the statement “Reports of overall findings or pooled analyses from published and unpublished in vitro, animal, epidemiological, or clinical studies must be submitted in a narrative format.” We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “in vitro, animal” with “nonclinical” in this sentence.
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 13. Section 312.32(c)(1)(v)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: List nonclinical studies and summarise nonclinical findings in the IND annual report
f.statement: 21 CFR 312.33(b)(6) is amended so that the IND annual report summary includes a list of the nonclinical studies (previously 'preclinical studies (including animal studies)') completed or in progress during the past year and a summary of the major nonclinical findings.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 14. Section 312.33(b)(6)
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: Section 312.33(b)(6) requires, as part of annual reports, a summary of information “obtained during the previous year’s clinical and nonclinical investigations,” including “[a] list of the preclinical studies (including animal studies) completed or in progress during the past year and a summary of the major preclinical findings.” We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “preclinical studies (including animal studies)” with “nonclinical studies” and replacing “preclinical findings” with “nonclinical findings.”
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 14. Section 312.33(b)(6)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: Include nonclinical toxicological findings in the NDA postmarketing annual report
f.statement: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(v) is amended so that the NDA holder's annual report includes copies of unpublished reports and summaries of published reports of new nonclinical toxicological findings (for example from mutagenicity studies) conducted or obtained by the applicant concerning the drug's ingredients; no new studies are required.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 8. Section 314.81(b)(2)(v)
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: Section 314.81(b)(2)(v) requires that the postmarketing annual report of an NDA holder include “[c]opies of unpublished reports and summaries of published reports of new toxicological findings in animal studies and in vitro studies (e.g., mutagenicity) conducted by, or otherwise obtained by, the applicant concerning the ingredients in the drug product.” The paragraph heading reads, “Nonclinical laboratory studies.” We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “toxicological findings in animal studies and in vitro studies (e.g., mutagenicity)” with “nonclinical toxicological findings, including, for example, from mutagenicity studies.”
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 8. Section 314.81(b)(2)(v)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: Give the initiation date of a nonclinical study in NDA postmarketing commitment status reports
f.statement: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(vii)(a)(7) is amended so that the status report of a postmarketing study commitment should include actual or projected dates for protocol submission, completion of patient accrual or initiation of a nonclinical (previously 'an animal') study, study completion, final report submission and other committed milestones; limited to postmarketing study commitments.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 9. Section 314.81(b)(2)(vii)(a)(7)
f.applicability: Postmarketing study commitments under approved NDAs
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “an animal” with “a nonclinical.” This change provides flexibility by recognizing that a postmarketing study commitment may include nonanimal nonclinical studies, and therefore, the status report should include the date for initiation of a nonanimal nonclinical study that is part of a postmarketing study commitment.
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 9. Section 314.81(b)(2)(vii)(a)(7)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.

f.title: Give the initiation date of a nonclinical study in BLA postmarketing commitment status reports
f.statement: 21 CFR 601.70(b)(7) is amended so that the schedule in a BLA holder's annual progress report for a postmarketing study commitment should include actual or projected dates including initiation of a nonclinical (previously 'an animal') study.
f.clause: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 4. Section 601.70(b)(7)
f.applicability: Postmarketing studies under approved BLAs (21 CFR 601.70(a))
f.exceptions: Not yet in force: direct final rule effective 4 February 2027 unless FDA withdraws it after timely significant adverse comments (comment period ends 7 December 2026). Until then the current wording ('animal or in vitro') applies.

rows.quote: We are amending the regulation by replacing the phrase “an animal” with “a nonclinical” in this provision. This change provides flexibility by recognizing that a postmarketing study commitment may include nonanimal nonclinical studies, and therefore, the status report should include the date for initiation of a nonanimal nonclinical study that is part of a postmarketing study commitment.
rows.location: V. Description of the Direct Final Rule - 4. Section 601.70(b)(7)
rows.review_note: Review: amended regulatory text; FDA states the rule adds no new requirements (terminology only). Double-check: pending (effective 4 Feb 2027, may be withdrawn); held below 90 until the effective date is confirmed.
